title: Comparison: Legislative Assembly vs Legislative Council

blocks.content: The Legislative Council is not an equal co-partner with the Legislative Assembly in state governance; it is designed to be a secondary and advisory chamber.

rows: Lower House / Directly elected by citizens
Upper House / Indirectly elected and nominated
Exclusive power to introduce and pass Money Bills
Cannot reject Money Bills; max delay of 14 days
Term of 5 years; subject to early dissolution
Permanent body (1/3 retire every 2 years); can be abolished

items: Only 6 states currently have a bicameral legislature: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
Unlike the Rajya Sabha at the Centre, the Legislative Council can be completely abolished by Parliament under Article 169.
The total maximum period a Legislative Council can delay an Ordinary Bill is 4 months (3 months in the first instance and 1 month in the second instance).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the popular house representing directly elected representatives of the state electorate.
The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is an upper chamber composed of indirectly elected and nominated representatives.
Under Article 169, Parliament has the power to create or abolish a Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.
The maximum strength of the Legislative Council is limited to one-third of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, with a constitutional minimum of 40 members.
The Legislative Assembly holds supreme financial authority; the Legislative Council can only delay a Money Bill for a maximum of 14 days.
